Mozem Par & Others

full_judgment: 8. In the instant case, there are facts which are not disputed by either of the party namely that the original tenancy belonged to the plain-tiffs predecessor Janab Ali Biswas and that he took Taka 200/00 from defendant Jaha Baksha Par and thereafter the patta was executed (Ext. A) Which was of the year 1953 and that it clearly showed the creation of a lease of the tenanted land by Janab Ali Biswas, the loanee in favour of loner Jaha Baksha Par. According to plaintiff-respondent Taka 200/00 was obtained as loan only and not as salami and that though Ext. A, the patta recites a lease in favour of defendant executed in the year 1953 by the plaintiffs predecessor Janab ali Biswas, the transaction indeed was an usufructory mortgage with a condition of reconveyance and not a lease though the plaintiffs predecessor had received rent from the defendant by granting dakhila and though defendant’s name was recorded in the Revisional Record of Right as a tenant. The defendant appellant on the other hand contended that there was no oral agreement. There was only one agreement and that was the patta duly registered and nothing more and nothing less. Further, that this registered patta was acted upon by the plaintiff's predecessors by accepting rents from the defendants by granting dakhila and it was further acted upon by the inclusion of the defendant appellant's name as tenant in the relevant S.A. Khatian and hence the terms of the document granting lease cannot be varied by oral evidence.
